results.evidence: Real contradiction: itinerary days and timing.sectionBreakdown describe the Elwha/Whiskey Bend/Long Ridge/Mount Fitzhenry approach, while approach, approach_variants, descent_text, waypoints and trailhead describe Sol Duc/High Divide/Carrie. Both approaches genuinely exist (the Fitzhenry line ascends brush and ridges over Fitzhenry to Fairchild's north glacier remnant; the Sol Duc line goes via the High Divide, Catwalk and Carrie). Fixing it means rewriting all four itinerary days (miles, gain, loss, hours, schedules) and the timing breakdown for the Sol Duc line, and no sources give day-level figures for a Sol Duc out-and-back to Fairchild, so no patch is written. Recommend a sourced rewrite of itinerary + timing to the Sol Duc line (or relabelling as a separate Fitzhenry variant).

results.correct_value: Sol Duc -> High Divide -> Cat Basin -> Catwalk (not Appleton Pass)
results.evidence: Real: waypoints[2]/[3] route via the Appleton Pass Trail and leave trail at Appleton Pass, while approach/descent go over the High Divide to Cat Basin. The fix needs the two pins moved/replaced (lat/lng are out of scope for this pass), so no patch; flag for pin rework of waypoints[2], [3] and the Appleton mention in waypoints[1].note.

results.correct_value: The Catwalk is the narrow exposed ridge between Cat Peak and Mount Carrie; the loose sidehill across Carrie's south face is a separate stretch beyond it.
results.evidence: One trip report calls the Catwalk a section of narrower ridgeline between Cat Peak and Mt. Carrie; an independent 8-day trip report describes it as a 1-2 ft wide rock arm between Cat Peak and Mt. Carrie. The row's waypoints, hazards and bivy notes already agree; only the approach and descent_text mislabel the Carrie south-face sidehill as the Catwalk.

results.correct_value: The Fairchild Glacier crossing from Carrie is crevassed and should be roped.
results.evidence: One trip report, descending the snow berm off Mount Carrie toward Stephen Lake, notes nasty crevasses on the north side of the berm and ropes up; another describes the glacier below Carrie as full of blue ice with crevasses they rappelled to avoid. Both contradict 'snowfields rather than a crevassed glacier'; the row's hazards, gear, waypoints and approach already call for roped glacier travel.

patches.find: Minor/localized - the route crosses lingering snowfields near the summit rather than a heavily crevassed glacier hidden crevasses or moats are possible especially earlier in the season before snow consolidates, so glacier-travel awareness is still warranted
patches.replace: Real - the line drops from Mount Carrie onto the Fairchild Glacier, which has open crevasses beside its snow ridge and turns to hard blue ice late in the season; hidden crevasses are likelier early, before the snow consolidates, so travel roped

patches.find: Basic glacier/crevasse-hazard awareness for the snowfields near Fairchild

results.correct_value: Olympic NP entrance pass; wilderness permit reserved in advance (no self-issue at trailhead).
results.evidence: The park's wilderness page says all permits are made through Recreation.gov, paper self-registration at trailheads is no longer available, Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin is a quota area and Bailey Range cross-country trips are booked by phone with the WIC. The park fee page and an independent Sol Duc trail guide confirm the park entrance fee (checked on Sol Duc Hot Springs Road) covers trailhead parking; a Northwest Forest Pass is a Forest Service pass and not what Sol Duc requires.

patches.find: Northwest Forest Pass required, self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk.
patches.replace: Olympic National Park entrance pass required; overnight trips need a wilderness permit reserved in advance, since none are issued at the trailhead.
